hotContext.criticalNews: Political/tax track advanced but not closed: Grimes County school boards approved eight SpaceX Terafab JETI deals (5-2 each) on July 14; Governor Abbott’s required decision was still unannounced after the July 15 deadline as of July 16 reporting. Separately, Samsung disclosed (via deleted LinkedIn post) AI5 process tape-out for 2nm at Taylor, with volume still mid/H2 2027—not a Terafab self-fab milestone.

recentKeyChanges.title: Grimes County School Boards Approve $119B Terafab JETI Tax Deals 5-2 Amid Local Opposition
recentKeyChanges.description: On July 14, 2026, Iola ISD and Anderson-Shiro CISD each voted 5-2 to approve all eight JETI school-property-tax agreements for TeraFab AI, LLC (SpaceX special-purpose entity) covering the proposed Terafab semiconductor complex near Gibbons Creek in Grimes County. Agreements grant a 10-year school M&O tax reduction per phase (freeze at ~50% of appraised value) in exchange for claims of up to $119B total investment across four phases, 4,234+ direct jobs, and ~22,000 acres. Phase 1 alone was previously filed at ~$10.37B; media also cite a ~$55B first-phase scale. SpaceX told districts that without the deals the project would likely relocate out of Texas (Arizona cited). Community opposition was strong over water use, noise/lighting, and loss of small-town character (Iola population ~300). School boards framed approvals as keeping the process alive, not final endorsement. Construction still needs Governor Abbott approval, three-party signing, and Comptroller filing—no permits or groundwater apps were on file as of mid-June reporting. SpaceX wants Phase 1 construction before year-end 2026.

positive_signals: Both Iola ISD and Anderson-Shiro CISD approved all eight JETI agreements (required school-district step)
Applications claim up to $119B investment and 4,234+ jobs across four phases
SpaceX stated intent to begin Phase 1 construction before end of 2026 if deals close
District leaders argue residual tax revenue still funds teachers and programs even with abatements
negative_signals: Votes were only 5-2—not consensus; public comment was largely opposed (water, identity, trust)
Deal is not final: still requires Governor Abbott approval and three-party execution before construction
SpaceX openly threatened to leave Texas without tax breaks—leverage, not manufacturing progress
As of June document reporting: no building permits, no groundwater applications filed despite 2026 construction claims
Project entity is TeraFab AI, LLC under SpaceX filings—not a proven Tesla-operated fab with semiconductor experience
Tax abatements transfer cost to state/local taxpayers; they do not solve talent, yield, or process-node execution risk
Geographic focus is Grimes County (Gibbons Creek), not demonstrated North Campus Austin fab groundbreaking

recentKeyChanges.title: Gov. Abbott Terafab JETI Decision Deadline Passes With No Public Yes/No; Deal Still Not Locked
recentKeyChanges.description: Under Texas JETI rules, Governor Greg Abbott shared the same 30-day window as the school districts after Comptroller acceptance on June 15, 2026—closing July 15. After the July 14 school-board approvals, KBTX reported on July 16 that Abbott’s decision remained unknown past the deadline. Law allows up to seven additional days to formally notify parties, so an answer could slip into the following week. If Abbott votes no, the school approvals are void and the deal dies; SpaceX filings state the project could leave Texas without the agreements. If yes, parties must still formally sign and file with the Comptroller before Phase 1 construction can start. Separately on July 16, Grimes County commissioners tabled a local ‘accountability’ resolution meant to set clearer industrial-project standards (water, lighting, noise, transparency)—signaling unresolved community and governance friction even as tax deals advance.

positive_signals: School-district approvals cleared one of two required political gates
Governor has a short additional notification window rather than an automatic rejection
County pause on accountability resolution was framed as allowing more public input, not killing the project
negative_signals: Abbott decision unknown after statutory July 15 deadline—project remains in limbo
A single gubernatorial no kills all eight school agreements regardless of 5-2 board votes
SpaceX has conditioned Texas siting on tax breaks; failure risk is explicit in filings
No public confirmation of Abbott yes by July 17 coverage—timeline for year-end construction already under pressure
Grimes County tabled manufacturer accountability resolution amid damaged public trust and water/noise concerns
Political process progress is not equivalent to fab equipment, process qualification, or first wafer
